question: Romanian industry was hit hard by high energy prices in 2022 and 2023. According to Eurostat, electricity prices for non-household consumers in Romania were higher than the EU average in the first half of 2022, being the fourth highest in the EU. Company closures and reduced activity were the immediate consequences of the energy crisis, with sharp drops in energy-intensive industries (22.1 % for chemicals, 15.
1 % for metalworking). Moreover, the electricity and gas price caps agreed by the Romanian Government in December 2022 are significantly higher than those in place in other Member States.

All things considered, there is general concern about deindustrialisation and the failure to prioritise the safeguarding of Romania’s strategic industrial players, as neither objective features in any of the national government’s plans and strategies. 1.

How is the Commission incentivising Romania to take a stand against deindustrialisation and invest better in the development of its national industries, and what programmes, guidelines and funds are in place to support Romania in this regard?

What is the Commission’s assessment of the government’s performance on safeguarding and developing Romanian industry and attracting foreign investment for industrial development? What are its recommendations for improvement?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.5.2024) The Commission treats strengthening the EU’s industrial base as a priority. To this end, an updated Industrial Strategy1 was adopted in 2021 and the Green Deal Industrial Plan2 in 2023.

The Net-Zero Industry Act3, the Critical Raw Materials Act4 and the Chips Act5 help direct EU and Romanian industry towards green, digital, and resilient investments in technologies and markets. Financing is available under the Recovery and Resilience Facility6 (EUR 28.

5 billion), Cohesion Policy funds (including EUR 115 million from the Sustainable Development Programme7 2021-2027 specifically dedicated to the creation of a financial instrument to support energy efficiency investments by enterprises), the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform8 or InvestEU9.

Romania’s industry accounted for around 22% of the gross value added generated by Romania in the last three years10 (2021-2023). The country is attractive to Foreign Direct Investments (FDI), which were above EUR 100 billion in 2022, 40% of which went to industry.

Insights into the priority areas for the Romanian economy are contained in the European Semester country report for Romania11 as well as in the Annual Single Market and Competitiveness Report12. Implementing the reforms and investments contained in Romania’s recovery and resilience plan and the European Semester will improve the business environment and contribute to attracting further FDI.
